subject: Shiny server open source edition in a work setting?

messages.author: bac0349c6d71ed28
messages.subject: Shiny server open source edition in a work setting?
parts: I've been showing Shiny apps at work and they really like the idea of using it for some of our simple internal tools and reporting. However, I think the price tag of the pro edition will be large barrier (at least until they've used it for a bit and seen it's value). What's the feasibility of using the open source edition in a work setting? The apps will be used for things like summarizing csv reports in to graphs, simple tools for constructing tracking URLs etc. They are currently using excel spreadsheets for all of this, but it's a big mess with different versions floating around. Having it online would be a big benefit for them. Thoughts?

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server open source edition in a work setting?
parts:
I've use shiny server open source on sites that get substantial traffic without any issues.  There's no reason it wouldn't be up to the task in a work environment from a performance stand point.  Server Pro offers some security and analytics features you'll be giving up, of course. But if you don't need those -- if you're just using it to display data etc. -- I don't see why not.  It's not hard to set up shiny server on a linux box so it's visible only to people on your network.  

Erik

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server open source edition in a work setting?
parts:
KJ,
As Erik mentioned, the open source version is definitely capable of handling the class of use cases you have described.  The Pro product is usually adopted by customers who need authentication, additional security capabilities, monitoring, and the ability to scale a single application to use multiple R processes.  If your business is a small or medium sized business we have special SMB pricing to make it more affordable for folks.  

-Tareef
